title: Entropy-gated continuous batcher: admission scoring + shaped filling to reduce tail spikes
creator: Alex Kim
description:
Problem: We see recurring p99 spikes during mixed prefill/decode workloads when large, high-entropy requests arrive that cause suboptimal kernel choices and large KV cache pressure. Current continuous batching admits requests largely on queue-age and simple size heuristics which permits pathological mixes that blow out tail latency. Goal: reduce p99 by ~30% under representative tail events (heavy long-context + high-entropy prompts) without regressing p50 and keeping cost within +10% of baseline.

Proposal (high level): Implement an entropy-gated admission scorer and batch shaper: 1) compute a lightweight per-request "admission score" combining estimated decode cost, entropy estimate (prefix surprisal proxy), and kernel-affinity delta; 2) use the score to gate admission when queue congestion crosses thresholds and to form shaped batches that bias homogeneous kernel affinity; 3) introduce a low-latency prefill hint path so prefill-heavy requests can be scheduled to a prefill-specialized slot pool while short/low-entropy decodes are routed to fast-path accelerators.

Why this is different: existing approaches focus on window sizing or static kernel affinity; the entropy-gated scorer explicitly considers the expected sampling complexity (rough proxy for KV/cache churn and decoder throughput) and uses that to avoid admitting high-cost items into mixed batches that would force slower kernels or cause re-kernelization.

Success criteria (metrics):
- p99 latency on mixed workload <= baseline p99 * 0.7 during synthetic tail bursts
- p50 change <= +5%
- End-to-end cost delta <= +10% for typical traffic profile
- No increase in error rate or non-deterministic behavior for deterministic models

Rollout plan: local sim -> internal canary on dedicated pool -> 5% Hosted API ring -> 25% -> 100%. Monitoring dashboards and automatic rollback threshold (p99 increase > 10% versus baseline) will be configured before canary.
acceptance_criteria: Admission scorer implemented and gated by config flag
Batch shaper groups by kernel-affinity at admission time at 90% accuracy for synthetic workload
Canary on dedicated pool demonstrates p99 reduction target in 2/3 experiments
Observability: new dashboard (prefill/decodes per admission-score bucket) and alerts for regressions
Clearfallover policy: automatic fallback to current admission heuristics on threshold breach
notes: 2026-03-10: Spike discovered during synthetic long-context burst test; correlated with kernel fallback to slow attention kernel (issue traced to kernel-selector threshold).
2026-03-11: Quick experiment: rejecting top-10% estimated-entropy requests reduced median throughput but lowered p99 by ~18% in the experiment cluster.

2026-03-12: Design review with Runtime team (Mateo Ruiz, Chen Li). Consensus: use cheap entropy proxy (prefix cross-entropy using last-layer logits sampled from recent model runs) to avoid per-request full forward cost. Need safety cap to avoid over-rejection under bursty small-request traffic.
2026-03-13: PR #4123 opened implementing scorer and the admission gating config. Initial unit tests and integration harness added. Requires kernel-selector API change (kernel affinity hints).
2026-03-14: PM review (Jordan Blake) requested explicit A/B plan and customer impact note; added canary rollouts and rollback thresholds in acceptance criteria.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive gating could increase p50 or drop throughput. Mitigation: start with conservative gating and run traffic-simulated tuning; expose weights as runtime-configurable feature flags.
Risk: Entropy proxy misestimates for uncommon model families. Mitigation: per-model calibration and fallback to size-only gate if calibration missing.
Risk: Kernel-affinity hints could be ignored by older runtime nodes. Mitigation: compatibility shim and rank-based fallback where nodes without hint accept based on old heuristics.
Risk: Increased engineering surface area and monitoring noise. Mitigation: phased rollout, unify metrics naming, implement sampling of raw request traces for debugging.
decision_log: 2026-03-12: Decided to use a 3-term admission score: (estimated_token_decode_cost * 0.6) + (entropy_proxy * 0.3) + (kernel_affinity_delta * 0.1). We will make weights configurable.
2026-03-13: Decided NOT to change kernel selection policy in this ticket beyond admitting kernel-affinity hints; kernel tuning to follow in separate workstream.
2026-03-14: Decided to keep the default behavior unchanged behind a runtime flag and to gate rollout by canary experiments.
